title: Average the quantities too
hook: Mixing different quantities makes a simple average of unit prices misleading.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Compute a quantity-weighted average rather than averaging unit prices blindly.

misconception: A mixture’s average unit price is always the simple mean of its labels.
objective: Compute a quantity-weighted average rather than averaging unit prices blindly.

claims.text: Material A costs €3/kg and B €6/kg. Compare 1kg of each with 2kg A plus 1kg B. Scaled model; fictional prices; additive masses; no mixing guidance.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Cheap-mass=2kg, A=4.5€/kg and B=4€/kg. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=4.5; B=["/",["+",["*",3,"x"],6],["+","x",1]]; x denotes Cheap-mass. At x=2, A=4.5, B=4; recall at x=5: B=3.5. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Total price divided by total mass weights each unit price by its quantity. The simple mean of €3 and €6 only describes equal masses. A larger share of the cheaper material shifts the weighted mean downward.

recall.question: Material A costs €3/kg and B €6/kg. Compare 1kg of each with 2kg A plus 1kg B. Change only Cheap-mass to 5kg. What is B (Chosen-weights) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Cheap-mass=5kg: it gives 3.5€/kg. Total price divided by total mass weights each unit price by its quantity. The simple mean of €3 and €6 only describes equal masses. A larger share of the cheaper material shifts the weighted mean downward.
